chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Ruzayq Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A group of people came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Our lands have suffered from drought, and the years have succeeded one another upon us, so supplicate to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, to send the sky (rain) upon us.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered the pulpit to be brought out, the people gathered, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ascended, supplicated, and ordered the people to say 'Ameen'.

It was not long before Jibra'il descended and said, 'O Muhammad! Inform the people that your Lord has promised them that He will send rain on such and such a day, and at such and such a time.' So the people did not cease waiting for that day and that time until, when that time arrived, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, stirred a wind, which raised clouds, covered the sky, and released the rain.

So those same individuals came in person to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah for us to withhold the sky (rain) from us, for we are on the verge of drowning.' So the people gathered, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) supplicated and ordered the people to say 'Ameen' to his supplication.

A man from the people said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, make us hear (your supplication), for all that you say, we do not hear.' So he (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Say: O Allah, around us and not upon us. O Allah, pour it in the depths of the valleys, and in the growth of the trees, and where the people of felt (nomads) pasture. O Allah, make it a mercy and do not make it a punishment.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْوَبَر: People of felt, referring to nomads or shepherds
key_terms.السَّمَاء: The sky, referring to rain in this context
key_terms.عَزَالِيَهَا: The release or letting down of the rain clouds

ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication taught by the Prophet for rain to avoid excess?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) responsive leadership, where he adjusted his supplication based on the community's feedback, specifically when a companion requested to hear the prayer clearly. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s role as an intercessor and the practical wisdom of asking for rain as a 'mercy' rather than a 'punishment,' reflecting the balance between divine decree and human agency in worship.

‘The people came to the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so they said, ‘O Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Our towns have drought and it has prevailed for years upon us. So supplicate to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High to Send the sky (to rain) upon us’. So the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> ordered for the Pulpit. They brought it out, and the people gathered. The Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> ascended and supplicated, and ordered the people to say ‘Ameen’.

It was not long before Jibraeel descended and said; ‘O Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>! Inform the people that your<sup>saww</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> has Promised to them that He<sup>azwj</sup> would Make it rain on such and such a day, and at such and such a time’. So the people did not cease to look out for that day and that particular time, until that time came up. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Excited a wind, so it raised clouds which covered the sky, and released the rain.

So those individuals came with their rich ones to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. They said, ‘O Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup>, Supplicate to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for us to withhold the sky (stop the rain) from us, for we are about to drown. So the people gathered, and the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> supplicated, and ordered the people that they should say ‘Ameen’ upon his<sup>saww</sup> supplication.

A man from the people said, ‘O Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup>, make us hear it, for all what you<sup>saww</sup> are saying, we cannot hear’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said; ‘Say, ‘Our Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Around us and not upon us. Our Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Let it pour in the middle of the valleys, and in the growth of the trees, and where the shepherds pasture. Our Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!
